 JUDGMENT
Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Sri.Jayaram.N S/o Chikkanarasimhaiah .
Veena V vs Manjunatha P on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182186490/
1

That on 23.02.2023 at about 01.30 PM., Jayaram N was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-Q-409, in Hosakote-Malur road, near Gonakanahalli gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, wherein the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-53-AA-4152 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident.
In the accident Jayaram sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Autopsy was conducted at Hosakote Govt Hospital.
Petitioners have performed the funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that deceased Jayaram.N was aged about 58 years of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was doing agriculture work and was earning Rs.40,000/- p.m., and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.39/2023.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.1 is the of the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with the respondent No.2, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.1 has not chosen to contest the petition and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.

Respondent No.2 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased as such they are not liable to pay the compensation and interest and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1, produced and marked 13 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 13 and she is fully cross examined.
Respondent No.2 examined its official as RW-1 produced and marked 6 documents which are at Ex.D1 to 6 and he is fully cross examined.
6. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides.
Respondent No.2 counsel filed written arguments along with 9 authorities.
I have perused the same along with entire records.

The counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has relied on the following authorities:
1. (2017) 3 KCCR 2471- 2.

sentences.text:
7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 23.02.2023 at about 01.30 PM., Jayaram N was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-Q-409, in Hosakote- Malur road, near Gonakanahalli gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, wherein driver of the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-53-AA-4152 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident.
In the accident Jayaram sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?
2 Whether respondent no.2 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions and deceased died due to his negligent act as contended in the written statement.?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?

8 . After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1 & 2: In the affirmative Issue no.3: In partly affirmative Issue no.4: As per final order for the following:
REASONS Veena V vs Manjunatha P on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182186490/
3 9.

entities.text: REASONS Veena V vs Manjunatha P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner No.1 and wife of the deceased Jayaram.N, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, Iquest, IMV report, PM report, Final report, DL which are at Ex.P.1 to 8, & 13.
10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Anjinappa S/o Late Ramappa was the driver of the offending vehicle.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence act of the driver of the offending vehicle that is he dashed the two wheeler from the body of his tipper lorry.
Further Ex.P8 is the final reported filed after the through investigation wherein the deceased and the insured are arrayed as accused No.1 and 2.
It is true that respondent No.2 has issued the notice to respondent No.1 as per Ex.D.4, but he has not chosen to given the reply for the same.
The conduct of respondent NO.1 being abstained before this tribunal establishes that he has accepted his guilt and liability.

11. The final report which is at Ex.P8 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the deceased.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved.
Respondent No.2 has establish its contention as contended in the written statement.

12. Admittedly the accident occurred on 23.02.2023, petitioners have not tendered the evidence to substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,000/- has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2023.
13. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the deceased is 20.07.1968.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 54 years 7 months and 3 days.
Accordingly the multiplier 11 is applicable.
14. Deceased was married and self employee and after 50 years of age, accordingly 10% of the future prospectus has to be added towards monthly salary.
Deceased left behind 3 dependents accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

15. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs.16,000/-
10% added towards future prospectus Rs. 1,600/-
Rs. 17,600/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal expenses Rs. 5,867/- 4

Monthly income Rs.11,733/-
Veena V vs Manjunatha P on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182186490/
4 Rs.11,733 (income)X 12 (month) X 11 Rs.15,48,756/- (Multiplier )
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,48,756/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.

16. Loss of estate;
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.

17 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.
18. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.
In the present case petitioner no.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased and they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.1,20,000/- as compensation under this head.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

19. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl Compensation under the Head Amount No. 1 Loss of dependency Rs.15,48,756/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs.1,20,000/-
In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.16,98,756/-.
20. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
The respondent no.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and respondent no.1 is the insured and owner of the offending vehicle.

The insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid as on the date of the incident and the driver and owner of the offending vehicle is not having valid DL as on the date of the accident as per the final report which is at Ex.P.8.

The insurer has probabilise the fact that insured was guilty of negligence and he failed to exercise the reasonable care in fulfilling the policy condition that is the use of the vehicle by a duly qualified licensed driver.

Accordingly insurer has successfully plead and proved the fact that the respondent no.1 has Veena V vs Manjunatha P on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182186490/
5 violated/ breach the fundamental policy condition and he knowingly and consciously handed over the offending vehicle and permitted/allowed the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the same without valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and it is the sole reason for the accident.

In the authorities relied on by the counsel appearing for respondent No.2 wherein the concept, pros and cons of the driver having no valid DL as on the date of the accident is categorically discussed.
Counsel appearing for petitioner has not tender any authorities.

With great respect to the aforesaid authorities and by considering the principles laid down therein and by considering the facts and attending circumstance, apparently there is the clear breach of the policy condition by the insured and it is the fundamental cause for the accident.
Accordingly the liability can not be attached to the insurer.
Inasmuch respondent no.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest to the petitioners.
Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 & 2 in the affirmative and Issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.16,98,756/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for Rs.5,66,252/- each in the total compensation amount with interest.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner No.1 to 3 are permitted to withdraw Rs.5,66,252/- each with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020, Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
